$comment: The gates a production promotion cannot skip, measured by scripts/check-deploy-gates.mjs against the workflow itself. Editing the workflow so a gate disappears fails this guard rather than shipping quietly.

requiredConditions.why: Without it a promotion runs on a commit whose CI went red.
Without it a branch that never merged can reach the production domains.
Without it a fork's CI run can trigger a promotion of the fork's commit.

gates.step: Wait for the staging verdict on this commit
gates.why: Production promotes an artifact staging already accepted; without this the first place a build runs is production.

gates.step: Verify the production schema ledger without mutation
gates.why: Code that expects a column the production schema does not have must not be promoted, and the check has to run before the build is deployed.

gates.step: Reconcile production env against the declared contract
gates.why: A missing production variable is a boot failure, and reconciling it after the deploy would find it too late.

gates.step: Require the protected Vercel deployment contract
gates.why: A deployment URL without protection is a second public origin serving unreleased code.

gates.step: Record the currently serving production deployment
gates.why: The rollback target has to be captured before the promotion replaces it; afterwards there is nothing to go back to.

gates.step: Canary the deployment before it takes the production domains
gates.runsBefore: Promote the deployment to the production domains
gates.why: A build that cannot serve a request must be caught on its own URL, not on the production domains.
The promotion is only complete when the production apex actually serves the promoted commit.

gates.step: Record the migration state this deployment serves
gates.why: Without it nothing durable says which schema the serving deployment was built against.

gates.step: Verify the promoted origin serves the repo's isolation headers
gates.why: The artifact sandbox is a separate origin whose whole safety property is its headers.

rollback.step: Roll back to the last verified production deployment
